$comment: Root ADR-0308. The release deploy's steps that ran in full on every deploy, whatever the release changed (the deploy of 77198c1f on 2026-10-27 spent 1 min 51 s migrating 48 lakehouse tables that release_changes.py had reported unchanged). Each step states either `inputs` -- paths under the Foundation Platform tree whose bytes make up what the step does, the shape config/worker-deploys.contract.json gives a Worker, read by scripts/deploy/deploy_steps.py with worker_autodeploy.py's fingerprint -- and is skipped while those bytes are the ones its last successful run on this host saw; or `always`, why it runs on every deploy, with `budget_seconds`, how long it may take before a line on stderr says it took longer. Which DAGs a deploy pauses and which running jobs it waits for or stops are not steps here: release_changes.py's hold list decides them (root ADR-0270 §3, ADR-0308).

postgres-chain.always: The runtime image is the release's own and carries its migrations (sqlx::migrate!), so the chain postgres, bootstrap, migrate, grants, finalize, api runs each deploy; the chain is run to completion before the API is replaced (2026-10-14) and is asked for as an end state, never with --no-deps (2026-09-02, scripts/guard/the-deploy-does-not-restate-the-compose-chain.sh), so compose re-runs its idempotent one-shots once per `up`. Measured 77 s on 2026-10-27.

start-once.always: Each short job orchestration/jobs.v1.json marks started_once_after_deploy runs once under the new release before the schedule returns (root ADR-0159 §4, ADR-0173): the first real input the release meets, while the deploy that brought it is still the one to blame. Measured 2 min 15 s for six jobs on 2026-10-27.
